key_insight: An analytical model links capacitance–frequency measurements to ionic relaxation and predicts the scan-rate window of maximum current–voltage hysteresis in perovskite solar cells.
engineering_relevance: Routine impedance measurements could provide a physically transparent, computationally efficient route to quantify ion migration and interpret device hysteresis.
method: Model the transition from low-frequency ion-screened depletion capacitance to high-frequency geometric capacitance, including interlayer effects.
Relate the characteristic transition frequency to the ionic dielectric relaxation time.
Connect capacitance–frequency response to scan-rate-dependent current–voltage hysteresis.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports excellent agreement with drift–diffusion simulations across varied ionic and transport-layer parameters, plus experimental confirmation of the predicted capacitance–hysteresis correlation.
watch_item: Parameter extraction should account for interlayer effects; the abstract does not specify experimental uncertainty or applicability across device architectures.
paper_title: Analytical Framework Relating Capacitance-Frequency Measurements and Hysteresis in Perovskite Solar Cells
